title: What to do if device space isn’t the issue

runs: Cancel the download in the Google Play Store, then restart the download.
If restarting the download doesn’t work, try logging out of >x<. Then retry downloading the app.
If you’re still unable to download the app, try uninstalling the >x< app from your device. After it’s uninstalled, restart your phone and then re-install the >x< app from the Google Play Store.

If you’re having trouble with the >x< for Android, first restart your device
Sometimes turning your device off and then on again can clear up any issues. If you’ve tried that and it didn’t work, try our other troubleshooting techniques.
Check your network connections
After powering down your device, make sure you have a strong data connection.
If you have a network connection but WiFi is turned on, your device will default to the WiFi connection.

If you’re using WiFi to connect to the >x< for Android app, try an alternate WiFi connection. If one works and the other does not, it is most likely that the WiFi connection does not accept SSL or is blocking >x<.
If you’re connected to a VPN, try turning it off. If turning off the VPN fixes your connectivity issue, you’ll need to contact your VPN provider for help.

Messages and other issues

If you're seeing Unauthorized or Invalid username and Password when you try to sign in, this is likely caused by incorrect time zone settings or an outdated version of the >x< client application. Please make sure your >x< client is up to date with the latest version and that the date, time and timezone settings are set to update automatically.
